To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of database clustering with a two-step PSI B-LAST search, and intermediate profile searches, improves distant homology recognition by more than 200% while using only 15-20% of the CPU-time of the standard PSI BLAST search.

(i) the granularity of sequence space affects the ability of sequence comparison methods to find remote homologies and (ii) sequence clustering strategies can improve remote homology recognition while reducing the search times of profile methods.

(a) database clustering and two-step profile searches improve the distant homology recognizations by 100% and speed up the searches by 10-fold; (b) intermediate profile searches improve distant homology recognition by 50% and speed up searches by 3-fold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the improvement of the sensitivity of profile searches, while at the same time speeding up the search process.
the improvement of sequence search strategies for remote homology recognition and fold recognition, which is an important step towards the automatic annotation of protein sequences and structures.
the improvement of profile-based sequence comparison methods.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the granularity of sequence space can be used to improve the speed and sensitivity of remote homology recognizations, but this improvement is only achieved when the granularity of sequence spaces is taken into account.
the granularity of sequence space can be used to our advantage in the design of more effective homology search strategies.
the granularity of sequence space can be reduced by clustering and that the resulting sequence clusters are useful for speeding up homology searches and for improving distant homology recognizations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the granularity of sequence space, and the resulting problems of uneven coverage, can be addressed with relatively simple strategies that are easily incorporated into existing profile-based sequence comparison methods.
the granularity of sequence space can be exploited to significantly improve remote homology detection.
sequence clustering and PSI-BLAST searches should be combined to achieve the best possible results.
